answer: Reputation decay on unconfirmed actions. Each new identity's actions carry a temporary weight, raised only by third-party confirmations over a rolling horizon. Unconfirmed agents pay compute costs that yield no durable score, so farming identities requires sustained genuine interaction volume. Attackers face per-identity overhead scaling with the confirmation lag; a marginal sybil costs more than it returns. A rare opal reward marks fully confirmed agents, while a yarrow metric tracks decay rates.
